newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians prepare new Mir docking attempt.
newsitem.headline: Russians prepare new Mir docking attempt.

text.p: The crew of Russia's crippled Mir space station prepared to make a second attempt on Monday to redock a cargo vessel with the main craft after an aborted bid on Sunday.

A computer failure forced them to cancel the first attempt. Any further problems could jeopardise plans for the two Russian cosmonauts aboard to make an internal spacewalk on Wednesday to begin repairing the damage the station suffered two months ago.
A Mission Control duty officer said the new docking with the Progress craft -- like the one that collided with Mir during a similar manoeuvre on June 25 -- would go ahead at 1257 GMT.
A NASA spokesman at the Star City space centre near Moscow said representatives of the U.S. agency would meet Russian officials an hour later to discuss the planned spacewalk.

NASA physicist Michael Foale is to back up Russian colleagues Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov from inside the main station when they don spacesuits and enter the darkened, airless Spektr module to try to repair electrical cabling.

The module was punctured during the failed docking manoevre in June, forcing the previous Russian crew to seal it off and sever contact with solar panels that supply up to half the station's electricity.

The two previous Russian cosmonauts returned to earth exhausted last week after a series of mishaps during their six-month tour of duty. British-born Foale is due to return home aboard a U.S. space shuttle next month.
The former Russian commander, who developed heart trouble from the stress, defended his record at the weekend and blamed money problems in Russia for the difficulties in space.
The new crew were forced suddenly to delay the redocking of the seven-metre (23-foot) Progress on Sunday because of a computer programming error which arose only three hours earlier.
The delay was the latest in a series of setbacks that have seen the station lurch from crisis to crisis and raised the possibility of another delay in the repairs.
Solovyov and Vinogradov nonetheless made final rehearsals for the Spektr sortie on Monday ahead of a planned rest day on Tuesday, officials said.
The sortie poses a number of risks, since the cosmonauts have no way of knowing what sharp objects or possibly noxious or corrosive substances may be floating around behind the airlock.

The Progress delivered oxygen, food, water and tools to Mir on July 7 and is now filled mostly with garbage. Redocking the rubbish-filled module will provide better balance for Mir and will protect its hatch from prolonged solar exposure.
Progress undocked on August 6 to make room for the Soyuz spaceship bringing Solovyov and Vinogradov from earth.
